title: Playbook / Rule Object Schema v1
description: Canonical schema for reusable decision-engine rule/playbook objects. Each playbook encodes one pattern: its trigger, diagnostic chain, recommended actions, guardrails, and expected impact. Playbooks are the machine-readable source of truth for what the engine detects, why, and what it does about it.

rule_id.description: Unique, stable identifier for this rule. Used as a foreign key in action cards and decision cards.

version.description: Semantic version of this rule definition (e.g. '1.0', '1.1').

module.description: Domain taxonomy locating this rule within the broader decision-engine module hierarchy.

primary.description: Primary module this rule belongs to (e.g. customer_retention, acquisition_efficiency).

channels.description: Data/marketing channels relevant to this rule (e.g. meta_ads, ga4, sms).

entities.description: Business entities involved (e.g. customer, product, campaign, ad_set).

context.description: Qualitative context about where and when this rule applies.

merchant_type.description: Description of the merchant archetype this rule targets.

applies_broadly_to.description: List of merchant types or scenarios this rule generalizes to.

products_in_scope.description: Product types or specific SKUs in scope for this rule.

problem_pattern.description: The observable business pattern this rule is designed to detect.

business_risk.description: Business consequences of this pattern going unaddressed.

observations.description: Optional quantitative baseline observations (before/during/after, or thresholds).

trigger.description: Conditions that must all be satisfied for this rule to fire.

metric.description: The metric or field being evaluated.

value.description: Threshold value (numeric) or reference metric name (string).

relative_to.description: Baseline or reference period the comparison is relative to.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of when and why this rule fires.

diagnostic_logic.description: Structured diagnostic chain: the ordered sequence of observations and implications that lead from detected pattern to root cause.

evidence_chain.description: Ordered chain of evidence steps. Each step is one inferential move from data to implication.

observation.description: What the data shows at this step.

implication.description: What this observation implies about the root cause or next diagnostic step.

data_source.description: Which data source or computation this observation comes from.

required_data_sources.description: Data sources needed to run this diagnostic chain.

minimum_viable.description: Minimum sources required to produce a RECOMMENDATION (vs HYPOTHESIS).

recommended.description: Additional sources that improve diagnostic confidence.

diagnosis_summary.description: One-to-three sentence plain-language summary of the diagnosis. This is the 'because' sentence the merchant sees.

likely_causes.description: Ranked list of likely root causes with individual confidence levels and supporting evidence.

cause.description: Plain-language description of this potential root cause.

confidence.description: How strongly the available evidence supports this cause.

supporting_evidence.description: What data or pattern supports this cause hypothesis.

checks_to_run.description: Ordered list of verification checks to run before acting (or to validate a hypothesis). If validation_status is HYPOTHESIS, these become the primary output.

why.description: Why this check is necessary before acting.

confirm_if.description: The condition that confirms this check passes (supports the diagnosis).

data_source.description: Where to find the data for this check.

suggested_actions.description: Priority-ordered list of recommended actions. Priority 1 is highest. All actions must pass preconditions before being emitted.

action_type.description: Machine-readable action identifier (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE). Must not appear in do_not_recommend.

recommendation.description: Specific, actionable recommendation text shown to the merchant.

preconditions.description: Named conditions that must be met before this action can be emitted.

automation_level.description: How much human approval is required before this action executes.

expected_impact_proxy.description: Expected business impact if the suggested actions are followed. Expressed as a proxy when exact ROI cannot be computed.

description.description: Plain-language impact statement tied to business outcomes.

key_metrics.description: Metric names that should move if the action is effective.

estimated_improvement.description: Directional estimate of improvement magnitude (e.g. '-15% CAC', '+20% repurchase rate').

do_not_recommend.description: Explicit list of action types that must never be recommended when this rule fires, with reasoning. This is a hard guardrail for the policy engine and LLM.

reason.description: Why this action must not be taken in this context.

common_ai_failure_modes.description: Known patterns where a weaker or un-grounded model is likely to produce incorrect diagnoses or recommendations. Used to harden LLM prompts.

failure_mode.description: Description of the failure pattern (what a weaker model would do wrong).

guard.description: The countermeasure: what to check or enforce to prevent this failure.

confidence.description: Overall confidence level of the diagnosis, given the available evidence. Drives validation_status: high/medium → RECOMMENDATION, low → HYPOTHESIS.

validation_status.description: Output mode for this rule instance. RECOMMENDATION = enough evidence to act. HYPOTHESIS = surface checks, not conclusions. INSUFFICIENT_DATA = required sources missing.

action_lever.description: The primary lever this rule pulls (e.g. replenishment_discount_nudge, ad_spend_reduction, landing_page_fix). Used for deduplication and lever-level budget controls.
